"Shall we go horse-riding on Saturday?" said Alistair.
Alistair suggested going horse-riding on Saturday.
"Don't touch the wiring!" he said to us.
He warned us not to touch the wiring.
"Let's have a barbecue tomorrow," said Peter.
Peter suggested having a barbecue the next day.
"You'd better go to bed now," he said to the youngsters.
He suggested that the youngsters should go to bed then.
"Shall I carry your cases?" he said.
He offered to carry my cases.

title: Special introductory verbs
instruction: Write an appropriate introductory verb, then report the sentence.
items: "You took my umbrella, didn't you?"
accuse - She accused me of taking her umbrella.
"I'll bring my report tomorrow."
promise - He promised to bring his report the next day.
"Get out of the workshop now!"
order - He ordered me to get out of the workshop.
"Don't forget to make a medical appointment."
remind - He reminded me to make a medical appointment.
"Please, please forgive me!"
beg - He begged me to forgive him.
"I won't sign it."
refuse - He refused to sign it.
"Would you like to travel with us?"
invite - He invited me to travel with them.
"If you do that again, I'll report you."
threaten - He threatened to report me if I did that again.
"I didn't break the mirror!"
deny - He denied breaking the mirror.
"First turn this dial, then press the button."
instruct - He instructed me to turn the dial first and then press the button.
"Yes, you were correct."
agree - He agreed that I was correct.
"What about going for a swim?"
suggest - He suggested going for a swim.
"You should take more exercise."
advise - He advised me to take more exercise.
"You mustn't touch the microscope."
forbid - He forbade me to touch the microscope.
"Don't cross the track without looking both ways."
warn - He warned me not to cross the track without looking both ways.
"Would you like me to feed your cat?"
offer - He offered to feed my cat.
"Yes, it was me who broke the kettle."
admit - He admitted breaking the kettle.
"I met the ambassador once, you know."
boast - He boasted about having met the ambassador.
"You always leave the kitchen in a mess!"
complain - He complained about my always leaving the kitchen in a mess.
"You must stay until 6 o'clock every day!"
insist - He insisted on my staying until 6 o'clock every day.

title: Subjunctive
instruction: Give the correct form of the verbs in brackets. Some are passive.
items: It is imperative that we ... (obey) his orders to the last letter.
should obey / obey
He insisted that he ... (pay) for the tickets.
should pay / pay
He proposed that apprentices ... (admit) into the association.
should be admitted / be admitted
It is important that you ... (take) these tablets twice a day.
should take / take
He demanded that no one else ... (allow) to see the file.
should be allowed / be allowed
She recommended that we ... (stay) at the smaller hotel.
should stay / stay
